name: reverse-inplace
axis: in-place reverse — two cursors walking toward each other; 2 bounds-checked reads + 2 bounds-checked writes per iteration with no arithmetic to hide them behind
n: N=4000000 i32 (16MB), ROUNDS=400 (800M element swaps' worth of accesses)
nPython: N=4000000, ROUNDS=25 (16x fewer rounds; multiply Python's wall time by 16 to compare)
notes: Hand-written two-pointer swap, NOT slice::reverse / Array.prototype.reverse / list.reverse. One element is incremented at the start of every round so that 'reverse twice is the identity' does not hold and no round can be folded; the result is consumed by summing every 65536th element (61 reads per round, negligible). Extra file `toplevel.vl` is the SAME algorithm written as a top-level script (module globals instead of function locals), the second data point for the globals cliff. Scale-verified by doubling ROUNDS: vl 1.98x, rs 1.95x, js 1.66x (JS's ratio is depressed by its fixed 4M-push setup), py 1.98x.

audit.rustVectorised: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT — rustc -O AUTO-VECTORISES this loop and no meta note said so. Confirmed by disassembling `main::main`: the hot loop is SSE2 packed integer arithmetic (18 packed ops). rustc's default target is baseline x86-64, so this is 128-bit SSE2; `rustc -O -C target-cpu=native` widens it further. The Rust:VL multiple on this benchmark is therefore mostly SIMD WIDTH, not scalar codegen quality — VL emits no SIMD. Report it as such.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
